subject: Keystone: urgent resilience summit — latency, errors, throughput impact
messages:
From: Sana Roy <sana.roy@keystone.ai>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@keystone.ai
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike affecting checkout (Keystone)

Hi David / Marissa —

We hit a significant regression on our Redwood endpoints starting ~08:45 PDT. Symptoms:
- 3–4x p95 latency increase (from ~180ms to ~720ms)
- Error rate on token generation requests spiked from 0.5% to ~6% for ~20 minutes
- Overall throughput dropped (requests queued, visible backpressure in our app)

This is impacting our checkout flows and causing retries. We rolled back no changes on our side; the only observable thing is a spike in long-token requests for a small cohort of users. Attached is a sampled metrics CSV and a short trace.

Can Redwood confirm whether there was any model variant or routing change on your fleet? We need an urgent call and an initial mitigation plan.

Thanks —
Sana Roy
Sr. Product Manager, Keystone AI
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Roy <sana.roy@keystone.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-04T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike affecting checkout (Keystone)

Sana — thanks for the quick heads up and the CSV. We're standing up an executive-level war room now.

Immediate actions:
1) Can you confirm the HubSpot ID or internal incident link and share any full traces you have?
2) We're going to look at routing, model-variant assignment, and cache saturation. Karthik and Grace are on infra and runtime.
3) Proposed 10:00 AM PDT call — will send a calendar invite in the next 5 minutes.

We will aim to provide an initial mitigation within the hour (fallback route and temporary model pinning) and a clearer timeline in the call. I'm CC'ing Marissa for customer comms and exec coordination.

— David
David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Cc: Tom Bishop <tbishop@keystone.ai>, ops@keystone.ai

Thanks, David. HubSpot ticket HS-8421 and our incident Slack channel are linked in the Drive folder. Sharing the detailed QPS/time CSV (attached).

We can join the 10:00 AM call. From our side: we noticed the traffic pattern shifted to longer conversations (avg tokens/request up ~2.1x) — not something recent on our side.

Sana
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-04T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (Internal) Keystone latency — quick triage notes

Internal quick triage: initial telemetry shows a KV cache saturation event on the cluster serving keystone-us-west. Key signals:
- Elevated KV cache miss ratio coincident with p95 jump (08:42–08:58 PDT)
- Spike in model variant "redwood-medium-qa-v1" requests routed to a subset of nodes with degraded GPU memory utilization
- Autoscaler created additional pods but they joined with cold KV cache and experienced higher latency on warmup

Short-term mitigation I'm pushing now:
• Force fallback routing to the alternate compatible variant (redwood-medium-qa-v1 -> redwood-small-quant) for non-sensitive routes
• Flush local per-node KV tier on affected hosts and allow controlled rewarm with rate-limited traffic

Attached: kv_cache_runbook_patch.diff (small helper to speed forced eviction), and a one-pager of the steps I'm executing. Will update in 10m.

— Karthik
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Roy <sana.roy@keystone.ai>, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-04T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Keystone: urgent resilience summit — customer commitments and exec ask

Hi Sana / team — quick customer-facing summary from Redwood execs:

What we saw: brief KV-cache warmup/backpressure causing elevated latency and transient error rate for requests hitting a specific node set.
What we're doing (committed):
- Immediate: fallback routing to less-memory-heavy model variant (in progress)
- Near-term (1–2 hours): controlled cache eviction and rewarm, temporary throttling on heavy long-token request cohorts
- Follow-up (24–72 hours): postmortem, quantize cost/perf tradeoffs for cache sizing, and schedule a joint runbook review with Keystone Ops

Customer ask: Marissa confirms Redwood will keep an exec-level line open for two business days and provide a rolling update cadence (every 2 hours while unstable). We'll also evaluate a goodwill credit if the SLA threshold was breached. Lauren and Sean — please prepare the renewal/credit impact and an exec-ready one-pager.

Sana — can you confirm whether you want us to apply fallback for all checkout routes or only non-authenticated QA flows?

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Roy <sana.roy@keystone.ai>, Tom Bishop <tbishop@keystone.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-05T15:33:00-07:00
Subject: Keystone incident: interim resolution, actions taken, and next steps

Sana / Tom — final status update from Redwood's war room:

Summary:
- Mitigation applied (04/04 10:05 PDT): fallback routing + controlled KV eviction + throttling on identified long-token cohort
- Observed outcome: p95 returned to baseline (~200ms) within ~18 minutes of mitigation; error rate back to ~0.7%
- Throughput: queued requests cleared; no further backpressure observed after rewarm window

What we did (short):
- Forced routing to compatible, lower-memory model variant for non-sensitive paths
- Applied a targeted KV eviction patch to speed warmup and avoid large-scale cold starts
- Instituted temporary rate-limits for heavy sessions while caches rebalanced

Follow-ups and commitments:
1) Joint postmortem scheduled: 2027-04-06 11:00 PDT — will include engineering and Keystone Ops.
2) We will share the runbook, the patch diff, telemetry snapshots, and proposed cache sizing changes within 24 hours (Drive link above).
3) Marissa / Lauren will follow up on any SLA/credit decisions.

Please keep the channel open until 04/06 EOD; if you prefer we keep the support bridge open continuously for 48 hours, we can do that as well.

Thanks for the rapid cooperation — David
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
